claim: “We have seen (Ch. 8, §7.1) that prepositions can often be used to indicate position in both space and time: at the gate or at noon”.
evidence_summary: Ch. 8, §7.1 (p. 702) is “Similarities and differences between the temporal and spatial domains”, but it begins “When we turn to extent in time, duration”, and its parallels are starting-point, endpoint and overall extent. The point cited is made at the opening of Ch. 8, §4 (p. 679), which refers to this very section: “This extension is motivated by the clear parallels in the use of prepositions in the two domains (see Ch. 19, §5.4”. Temporal at, in and on are listed in §6.3 (p. 696).
finding: Change §7.1 to §4. The two passages cite each other once the reference is corrected. Ch. 8, §§4, 6 would also do, since §6 has the temporal prepositions. Checked on the page image while the errata list for the authors was being prepared.
inference: Does Ch. 8, §7.1 treat prepositions of position in space and time?

evidence.passage: §5.4, p. 1683. “We have seen (Ch. 8, §7.1) that prepositions can often be used to indicate position in both space and time”
evidence.establishes: The point is made in Ch. 8, §4, which cross-refers to Ch. 19, §5.4.
